Subject: Purchase options & security gating — PO vs Card vs Marketplace

Hi Samantha / Daniel,

Thanks again for the time today — good discovery. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Recap: NexaCare is evaluating Redwood for an initial pilot (clinical summarization) and a potential org-wide rollout in H1. Key gating items are procurement path and SOC 2 / DPA requirements.
- Procurement options we discussed: 1) pilot on card for < $5k, 2) direct PO for enterprise contract (annual commit), 3) AWS Marketplace for cataloged procurement and faster procurement ops.
- Security/compliance ask: you mentioned SOC 2 Type II and a signed DPA are mandatory prior to production access.

Can you confirm: 1) which procurement path you prefer for the pilot vs enterprise, 2) the internal procurement contact (I saw procurement@nexacare.com in the meeting notes), and 3) any additional security docs beyond SOC 2 & DPA (e.g., pen test, data retention policy)?

I’ve attached a short procurement checklist to make it easy to see what we can provide quickly. If PO is the preferred route, we’ll scope out the SOW & payment terms; if Marketplace, I’ll loop in Marissa to confirm listing details and fees.

Suggest 1:30pm PT on Thursday for a quick align with procurement if that works on your side — otherwise send their preferred cadence.

Thanks,

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Purchase options & security gating — PO vs Card vs Marketplace

Thanks Rishi — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot approach: we prefer to run the pilot on card if it stays under ~$5k total spend. This avoids PO processing for short pilots and lets our dev team iterate quickly.
- Enterprise rollout: for any production/RoI commitment we will require a PO and a 12-month term.
- Marketplace: we are open to AWS Marketplace if pricing and contract flow are standard — procurement likes the consolidated billing idea but needs to confirm fees and entitlements.

Security gating: SOC 2 Type II is required. We will need a redacted report (summary is fine) plus an executed DPA. We may also ask for an info-security questionnaire; if you have a standard completed copy we can start there.

Procurement contact: procurement@nexacare.com (I’m looping them above). They’ll want to see: SOC2, DPA, a sample SOW/terms for PO, and a contact for redwood to send a PO to once approved.

Timeline: procurement can turn around paperwork in ~10 business days once they have SOC2 + final pricing.

Looking forward to the checklist and SOC2 redacted copy.

—Sam
Samantha Cole
Head of Clinical Programs | NexaCare
